layers.label: Orbital mosaic colors · coarse display
limitations: NASA visualization color map optimized for aesthetics, not science; exposure/white balance adjusted and high-latitude gaps inpainted.
LROC color covers 70 N to 70 S; polar regions use lower resolution monochromatic LOLA albedo fill.
JPEG derivatives are display imagery, not scientific feature or similarity evidence.
Coarse display mosaic sampled by source longitude/latitude; approximate registration only, no independent tie-point alignment to local DEM.
Mosaic display frame and native DEM realization have not been transformed or independently registered; this is an illustrative image drape.
129-pixel output samples the existing orbital image; output size does not add source detail or ground resolution.
This south-polar location uses the published monochrome LOLA albedo fill, not a local color photograph; no color has been invented.

layers.label: Orbital mosaic colors · coarse display
limitations: Viking color mosaic sharpened with MDIM 1.0; source nominal 64 pixels/degree, about 920 m/pixel.
Global imagery has historical mosaic seams and is separate from the local HiRISE DTM; no global Mars displacement is supplied.
JPEG derivatives are display imagery, not calibrated photometry or a similarity score.
Coarse display mosaic sampled by source longitude/latitude; approximate registration only, no independent tie-point alignment to local DEM.
Mosaic display frame and native DEM realization have not been transformed or independently registered; this is an illustrative image drape.
129-pixel output samples the existing orbital image; output size does not add source detail or ground resolution.

layers.label: HiRISE local ortho · published grayscale
limitations: Published HiRISE ortho pixels retain original image illumination, shadows and display processing; no new contrast stretch or colorization.
Projected ortho and DEM are mapped through their declared CRSs; no independent tie-point or photometric calibration is claimed.
Published RED-channel image is grayscale; RGB channels repeat its gray value without invented color.
Nearest source-pixel sampling; texture and DEM spatial resolution remain distinct.
